The stated first three radial moments give cum3(Y)=8aP_d(a)/[d^2(a+1)^3(a+2)(a+3)(a+4)(a+5)]. The polynomial P_d has negative constant, all positive nonconstant coefficients for d>=1; it crosses exactly once, a_1=a_2=1, and P_d(1/2)=-9(6d-1)/8, P_d(1)=2(d-1)(d-2). For real d>=2, rewriting P=(4a-2)d^2+(3a^2-3a-6)d+a(a+1)^2 makes da_d/dd<0 at its zero. Independent symbolic cumulant factorization and numerical root checks reproduce the stated asymptotic limits. Independent thermal Gaussian convolution gives cum3(E)=cum3(Y)+12h Var(Y)+24h^2 E[Y]+8dh^3. For d=3 the cleared-degree-seven polynomial has strictly positive constant and degrees >=2 for h>0; only linear coefficient can be negative, so Descartes gives at most two positive roots. Strict increase with h, positive endpoints for h>0, and a nonempty negative interval at h=0 force a unique critical coalescence. Solving K=K_a=0 independently gives (0.13982748204004,0.01962977632358); finite checks only corroborate the analytical all-parameter argument.
